claim:
Let \(a,b>0\), and for \(0\le d\le \min\{a,b\}\) define
\[
n(a,b,d)=\inf_{0<t<\pi/2}\frac{a\sin t+b\cos t-d}{\sin t\cos t}.
\]
Put \(L=(a^{2/3}+b^{2/3})^{3/2}\) and \(\kappa=(ab)^{1/3}/(a^{2/3}+b^{2/3})\). Then \(d\mapsto n(a,b,d)\) is concave and
\[
n(a,b,d)\le L-\frac{d}{\kappa}\qquad(0\le d\le\min\{a,b\}).
\]
If \(a\ne b\), the inequality is strict for every \(d>0\); if \(a=b\), equality holds throughout the interval. Moreover, as \(d\downarrow0\),
\[
n(a,b,d)=L-\frac{d}{\kappa}-\frac{(a^{2/3}-b^{2/3})^2\sqrt{a^{2/3}+b^{2/3}}}{6(ab)^{4/3}}d^2+O(d^3).
\]
For all sufficiently small \(d>0\), this \(n(a,b,d)\) is exactly the largest possible long side of a rectangle of short side \(d\) that can move around each of the three ladder-limited corridors \(\mathcal C_{03},\mathcal C_{11},\mathcal C_{13}\) of Mushkarov--Nikolov. Thus the classical zero-width ladder length has a sharp finite-width linear loss, while corridor anisotropy contributes a strictly negative quadratic correction, vanishing exactly when \(a=b\).

correctness.rationale: Write the frontier as \(n(a,b,d)=\inf_t(G(t)-dH(t))\), where \(G(t)=a/\cos t+b/\sin t\) and \(H(t)=1/(\sin t\cos t)\). Concavity is immediate from an infimum of affine functions. The unique zero-width minimizer has \(\tan t_0=(b/a)^{1/3}\), yielding \(G(t_0)=L\) and \(H(t_0)=1/\kappa\), so evaluation at \(t_0\) proves the global tangent bound. For \(a\ne b\), \(H\'(t_0)\ne0\), making the bound strict for every positive width; for \(a=b\), the source exact formula gives equality. Nondegeneracy \(G\'\'(t_0)=3(a^{2/3}+b^{2/3})^{3/2}>0\) permits implicit differentiation, and the envelope formula gives the displayed negative second derivative. The equivalence \(d\le m(a,b,c)\iff c\le n(a,b,d)\), together with the source classification, proves the corridor interpretation for all sufficiently small \(d>0\). The packaged symbolic checker independently simplifies the critical identities and returns VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: The width-zero ladder length is a classical geometric threshold, and the 2026 paper makes its finite-width rectangle frontier exact. The new result quantifies the robustness of that threshold with a sharp global supporting line and the first nonlinear correction. The coefficient has a structural equality classification: the quadratic loss vanishes exactly for equal corridor widths and is strictly present under anisotropy. This is a natural boundary invariant of the solved feasibility region, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of a known table.
